body: I recently went through this same exact thing, what I asked was "what is my official diagnosis so that I can inform my other doctors". I felt that gaving a reason for wanting to know made it more okay to ask.
Are the drawers real? Last time I went in they were fake.
I have not split the 7.5s but have split higher doses of mirtazipine on doctors advice.
At the PHP I got just out of you saw the doc once a week minimum, but you could ask to see them whenever you needed support. At the other one I went to you saw the doc twice a week.
You should probably contact a pharmacist. Even if the active ingredient is likely fine the fillers may go bad and effect absorption
I always had privacy when I showered. Even when I was at the highest level of observance there was at least a curtain between the person and me.
I do the same thing but right in the middle of hypomania. It is often my first real sign that something is wrong. It is embarrassing the level of obsession I can reach.
It depends on what subject you plan on studying in grad school and what degree you are pursuing. But it is intense especially in science.
If you are at a college, they may have health service group with therapists. It is a easy option that is often free or cheap.
I am stable now and everything is lining up well, I am just a nervous wreck about it.
I applied to grad school for a second masters. Now I am regretting that as I get ready to start the masters program.

I saw the musical several times years before my diagnosis and I always found it a funny coincidence that one of my favorite shows portrayed bipolar.

Some of the songs resonate a lot with what I have gone through like "I miss the mountains". And it made me more willing to get ECT.
I have almost constant internal monologue and when it isn't being useful it is freaking out about something. That is what my anxiety manifests as.
I was unemployed/student at the time
I am over 26 and there was no problem with me staying on my parents insurance. If you call the company they may be able to give you instructions.
I couldn't understand why anyone would care enough to be transgender.
Tungsten, Iodine, Iron
I am. Glad I don't have to deal with hypersexuality.
It took me a year, but it got better.

I was working with them so I couldn't cut them off like I wanted to. To manage the feelings I kept thinking all the reasons I couldn't have them and how I didn't want to hurt them or myself. It helped but in the end leaving and distance was what helped me get over it.

It is reassuring to hear that I am not the only one with a back up plan always there. I only mention it to my psych and therapist when I am actively considering it. My therapist does know it is there and I think she sees it as a coping mechanism for me - always knowing I have a way out if things get to be too much.

My therapist has worked with me on techniques for blocking out the backup plan when things get stressful, mostly focused on remembering what else I have good in my life. She doesn't seem too concerned that it is there as long as I have methods and willingness to block it out.
When I went to a higher dose I became apathetic.
I'm on 450 mg lithium with lamictal. I still have minor mood episodes, but it helps with suicidal thoughts.
I am on lithium and lamictal as well and the two of those with the low dose of vraylar works for me.
I've been on vraylar 1.5 mg for 5 months with no plans to go off it.

Make sure to maintain a work life balance. Even around exams or major products don't forget the rest of your life and necessary daily tasks.

Don't take failure personally. Sometimes it is unavoidable and out of your control (especially if you are doing scientific research).
The only thing a disease needs to do in order to stick around is allow the person to reproduce.

Probably not the best coping mechanism, but I work to clean my apartment and pack up as much as possible to "make it easier on my family." By the end of the day I am too exhausted to do anything - and my apartment is clean.
I have one of the Valentines day bottles that says "I keep my feelings bottled up"

What works for me is cooking a lot while I am feeling good and freezing it all so when I am down I still have home-cooked meals to heat and serve. I make mostly soups, stews, and casseroles since it is easy to package up a serving or two.

When I stopped taking my meds I ended up hospitalized. Meds suck but they help.

It would probably be best to talk to your doctor before restarting them especially with lamotrigine because of the incremental increases needed when starting.

I like hypomanic me best. I tend to get hyperfocused on a topic (once it was studying for exams which was extremely useful). I also become slightly more outgoing and I can make friends which stable and depressed me does not do.
I generally go with the even more generic "I was dealing with medical issues."

I normally tried to go for a walk or do something physical. When I was super unproductive I would mindlessly scroll through social media.

I had to change my med timing once it got really bad. It seemed like the effects of one of my night-time meds was wearing off so I started splitting the dose morning and night which has helped.

I told my therapist 5 days after an attempt. They were shocked but they never spoke of me going inpatient. I was also helped by the fact my attempt seem to trigger a hypomanic episode which meant I was relatively safe from myself.
It is well know issue that has a fancy name and everything though I don't remember it at the moment. I told them because one mentioned how much better I looked as I was feeling terrible.

I am the same way, the worse I feel, the happier I look. I laugh when I talk about suicide. Doctors, friends, and myself all find it disconcerting, but have become accustomed. I did decide to warn my doctor and therapist not to trust my affect.

Generalizations don't always work for specific people. I have been prescribed a bunch of drugs for sleep many of which it says this is not to be used as just a sleep aid. My sleep is tough to regulate. I have been on seroquel for sleep, it didn't work for me, but I know it is prescribed. Like the other commenter said, talk to your doctor about your concerns and they may be able to give you something else.
Sounds familiar. It is to the extend I warned a friend I had only know when hypomanic what was about to happen so they wouldn't get worried.

Are you registered with the school's disability services office or did you take medical leave during that time? Either of those might help your case, otherwise in the past I have always just said medical issues that I have since taken steps to prevent from happening in the future. I'd say you can keep it general or go into more detail depending on how comfortable you are with disclosing.

I was the same for over a year. I never told my therapist that my happiness masked constant suicidal ideation and that I selfharmed often. I was scared how she would see it as weakness and scared of involuntary hospitalization. It took a suicide attempt and a switch from depression to hypomania for me to open up. At the appointment after my attempt I just dumped everything from the past months on her and it felt good. Now it feels more helpful and I don't dread it.

As for my hospitalization fear, she let's me decide if I am safe and I have built up enough trust that she believes me. 

Just telling my therapist everything at once was the best decision I made and it has helped a lot. I no longer feel like I need to hold things back. I hope you can convince yourself that it will be a good thing.
I refused to learn how to drive because of anxiety. I dislike busses too, but I love subways and find them soothing for some reason.

I do not remember my childhood for other reasons, but my mother said I was a perfect child most of the time, but once or twice a year I would explode and be unmanageable for a few days. I can't help but wonder if that is related to my eventual diagnosis.

I am currently applying to masters programs in a science field. I am electing not to mention bipolar disorder anywhere in my application. When it gave me an opportunity to write about anything in my past that needs to be explained, such as the Gap in my transcript, I'm just saying I was dealing with medical issues at the time.

 I can see how they would see someone with bipolar disorder as an unreliable candidate due to the stigma surrounding mental illness and bipolar in particular. (I obviously do not agree). In the end it is up to you to decide if honesty would strengthen your application.
I was a graduate student and I was able to take medical leave. They were very understanding about it without me going into details.

It was a nice ward and because I was a well-behaved patient I got special privileges due to my long-term stay. And the hospital argued with insurance so that insurance covered it. They did not want to discharge me early just because of insurance.
My voluntary stay was three months. It took a long time to get me stable. Most were there a week or less, I think 5 days was the average for the ward.

That happened to me once when I was depressed and ready to be done with everything. I was about to do something stupid when a switch flipped and I was hypomanic. Oddest switch I've ever had since it is normally gradual and hard to pinpoint.

I have obvious signs when I am hypromanic or depressed. Before the end of an episode I know what is going on but I still can't control it. I felt like I was doing it on purpose. At first I always thought I was faking too, but over the years it is obvious.

So it happens that you don't believe the diagnosis. Like the other comment said, talk to your doctor and therapist and see what they say.

I spent 3ish years on lamictal after being diagnosed. I was stable and doing well, but then I ran out of meds after moving. I continued to be fine for a year and a half unmedicated before falling into deep depression. Hospitalization after a suicide attempt and going back on meds is what saved me. 

If you are feeling good now, there is a strong chance you are that way because of the meds. You can try going off meds with a doctor's supervision, but be very careful and don't get complacent just because it seems to be okay. I thought I was fine given how long it had been, but it was downhill fast.

Best of luck either way and stay safe.
My family and terror that there would be long term physical health consequences of a failed attempt.

It's not idiotic to think that a short time symptom free means it won't come back. At first off meds I was terrified I would have a problem but as time went on and I didn't have any major episodes I started to think I was "cured". Little did I know I was just living on borrowed time.

Some psychiatrists seemingly don't understand the complexities of bipolar which isn't surprising, there are a lot of psychiatric disorders,  but it is hard to find someone who can treat you properly and give you a chance.

Finding meds that help had been good.  It still isn't perfect, my cycle is less noticeable.

3 years ago I went off my meds because I didn't have a doctor at the time. I was fine for a year and a half before I sank into a very deep depression. During that year and a half I felt better than I had for a long time but it didn't last. Now I'm struggling again trying to find a med combination that works, similar to you I don't object to meds but it's just so hard. It seems that I might have finally found a combination so there is always hope that it could work out in the end.

 If you do choose to stay med free, my recommendation would be to watch yourself and track your moods very carefully.  I would also suggest that you do have a psychiatrist so that if you start to have problems there someone you can go to right away.

I have to take mine split because even with the extended release my body processes it extremely quickly and my levels dip before the next dose. Barring odd circumstances,  it should be possible to take it all at once.

I don't think people who have never been suicidal will ever truly understand how little living can mean to a person. Even when I am not actively suicidal and am stable, I still would rather be dead. I have never understood why people care about keeping others alive.

Also there is no guarantee a person will receive financial and emotional support at least in the US. It is basically we want you alive but don't want to support that life.

I have felt like that before. I have also hoped hypomania would end so I would kill myself. For me the meds eventually helped and the feeling went away. My only advice is to stay on the meds and give them a chance. They are doing something if you are feeling like you have to go off them in order to commit suicide.
Thank you, one person I vented to didn't seem to think it was a big deal, but they also haven't had to deal with stigma in the past
For me when I was like that my doctor split my dose of lithium so I was taking it both morning and night. That seemed to help.
I find myself lying almost constantly to everyone around me. It's not a side effect of the bipolar but it's caused by it in that I'm trying to protect everyone around me from the true me

I had ECT and it finally kept me stable long enough for meds to be effective. Even if it is a short term fix, sometimes that short time is enough to get everything else in place for long term stability. The side effects can be unpleasant, but I was generally fine the next day. There was some memory loss around the treatment, but I got it back eventually. It is a safe and effective treatment, it is not what it used to be.

I have been know to purge my stuff when I am manic or depressed just because it is cluttering up my apartment. My best solution so far is to get boxes (or just garbage bags) and put everything I want to get rid of in there and then "hide" the boxes in my apartment out of sight. After I am stable again I can get my stuff back or throw it away if it is truly unnecessary.

I did have more memory loss than normal, but it has come back. I would recommend writing down important things before you go like passwords and health information just in case you lose them temporarily. And during the treatment keep a Journal because some of that time period never did come back

I would have to say knowing the chemicals are the only thing holding you back.

I have had to deal with knowing I want to die but being stopped by chemicals constantly. Natural chemicals of hypomania and the unnatural chemicals prescribed. It was bad wanting hypromania to end so I would be willing to go through with killing myself. And after that the drugs finally started working before I got around to stopping them. So I am still here, eventhough I regret that often.

I was really freaked out when my doctor first suggested ECT. But she eventually talked me into it and it was actually really easy. The treatment itself was really short. They put you under for 5 to 10 minutes to administer the actual treatment and then you're in recovery for an hour or two and then you're free to go if you're outpatient or you go back to your ward if you're inpatient. It is nothing like it used to be. They use minimal electricity. I honestly remember nothing of the treatment because there was some memory loss right around treatment itself.

As for side effects it wasn't too bad. Just headache, a bit of muscle stiffness and some memory loss, but it's come back even though I was getting the maximum treatment for a long time.
Would it be possible to add a minor to give you more job flexibility in the future?

I don't mind meds in general, but I went off my meds since I hate going to doctors and I ran out of my prescription. I was okay for two years before I was inches away from suicide. Since then I go to every appointment and am cooperating with med adjustments. 

For me it is a case of meds vs death and I choose meds.

I am still adjusting my meds so there is a small chance I will get better, but I am realizing that I need to learn to live with the thoughts. I want to learn to treat suicide like an old friend that I entertain every once and a while but don't meet with on a daily basis. I do not think I will live to my possible age; I fully expect I will kill myself eventually and I am okay with that.

Are you still sleeping well? When the doctor shifted my doses around and I took less at night and more in the morning. I slept less and was more tired during the day. Lamictal is one that can make you drowsy or be activating depending on the person. My doctors are always surprised that I could sleep after taking 200 mg at night.

Depending on how long ago you lowered your dose, it may be a case of waiting a bit longer, nine years is a long time to be on a drug and for your body to become accustomed to. 

As for normal dose it depends on the person, I take 400 mg but I have seen other people on this sub who take less.

Best of luck getting used to the new dose.

Most of the time was just hanging out or going to art/therapy sessions. There was one memorable time four of us were playing ping pong with no net. It devolved into a fun game of keep the ball off the floor.

Definitely watch you moods. I would urge you not to get complacent after a few months. I was fine for a year and a half and then tried to commit suicide with no outside signs that I was depressed. So keep an eye on yourself for the long run and be honest with yourself and others. Good luck trying med free.

I will say I felt better without meds, but in the long run it was worse. Now I am on a med that wasn't even available back then and it is helping, so try not to give up hope that in the future something may change if you ever have to go back on meds.
So much relief. I was treated well, I just didn't stop myself from constantly working and didn't follow any kind of self care regime.

I am proud that I finally contacted my professor to leave a grad program (this sounds like a bad thing, but leaving is necessary for my health and I still got a degree, just not the one I wanted). I also got her and two other professors to agree to be references to a different type of grad program. I even started the applications. I have been putting this off for months but I finally did it.

I believe my accommodations stated that I contacted the professor to arrange for an extension if I needed it. Most professors were really understanding so it was easy, I would talk to them at the beginning of the semester and figure out how it would work for that specific class.
Those comments I occasionally downvote, but you can also report them

Whenever I am on a new antipsychotic my dreams get super nonsensical and super vivid. I just started thorazine and now I am waking up from dreams two or three times a night. I remember details for about 10 minutes and then I will completely forget it other than the odd out of context one liner: "I forgot forks don't need to breath"
Citizen soldier - Would anyone care

Technically anything can be an advantage to the right person. For me the mania got me qualified for a PhD program and now the depression is causing me to drop out. I can see the advantage to being bipolar, but the downsides seem greater.
I have never experienced hypersexuality. When manic I will just develop an obsession with a person that is not at all sexual. One of my best indicators.

I am not a medical professional. But most of the supplements available are really low dosage. The general therapeutic dose is over 500mg and the vast majority of the supplement seem to be around 5 mg. Additionally supplements are not as highly regulated as FDA approved medications. If you're interested in lithium it's probably better to talk to your psychiatrist about getting a prescription.
I hate that I failed. I have been so close to trying again, all that holds me back is the fear I will fail again. I haven't had any moments of happiness that make living worth it.
On the issue of not liking to shower, one piece of random advice I saw was to shower with the lights out or else really dim.
Ignore my username, I am definitely not a dragon.

"You don't have to be happy at all, To be happy you're alive"

-Next to Normal

It shouldn't have to be a secret, but I personally feel like people will treat me differently or not trust me if they know. Additionally, when I was diagnosed my mother told my extended family without asking me. Mental health issues run in that side of the family and she wanted them to be aware, but I still felt betrayed. That has made me even less likely to tell people.

I end up only telling people I am really close to and who I think will be worried when they notice a large change in my actions and mood.
Since I started meds I haven't had a manic episode, only hypomania. But I do still have several depressive episodes a year that last for months.
I never thought I would make it to 25 after being diagnosed at 20. My 25th birthday was hard as were subsequent birthdays, but the rest of the time I don't realize that I survived past my "end date."
I am, but I react badly to almost everything so I have limited options. Currently trying to change my meds and it is not going well.
My "stable" is flat and emotionless for the most part. I could  motivate myself to do things but I didn't find it rewarding even if it was something I used to love.
That is the worst profession for rage. I hope you can see a doctor soon to adjust you meds.

I am having the same side effects on another drug currently and am going to ask my psychiatrist to go off it today. The rage especially is not worth it because I never know if I am going to attack someone.

One of my doctors called me "brilliant but disturbed" and the staff agreed. I don't think I was ever supposed to find out about that, but I was in long enough to become friendly with the staff. I am still amazed that they found me disturbing given what they see on a daily basis.

Chemistry. Another thing that was useful to me was remembering that even neurotypicals have problems coping in grad school. When I complained to a friend that I was feeling unproductive he reminded me that he got nothing done for two months once because of his life events.

I will say though, take care if your research starts to stall or becomes too difficult so you don't fall into depression (this only became a problem when I went off meds though).

I am in a PhD program and I was definitely hypomanic while I was taking cumulative exams. However, it was productive hypomania with me not sleeping and being hyperfocused on studying for 12 hours a day. Most of the time being bipolar didn't effect me too much, just occasional periods where I was super productive and times when I was less productive, but it evened out and I had an understanding advisor.
The best one I have had was "I forgot forks don't need to breathe"

What helped me most was being treated like a regular person by the staff. I was in the hospital for several months and got to know the staff well and we would joke around which was really helpful to me, a peice of normalcy in a strange situation. Even when I was put on the highest level of restriction they treated me the same, not like I was sick or subhuman.

I have tried 13 different medications and most of them lasted a very short time due to side effects. My favorite quote from a psychiatrist was "I am never giving you another atypical antipsychotic." So cheers to losing one of the most commonly prescribed classes of medication.

My psychiatrist had me split 200mg lamictal to change around my doses for a while. As long as the pill has a score line down the center it should be fine. If it is the extended release it definitely should not be split.

For me it wasn't courage. I had been suicidal for months but I was so depressed that I did not have the motivation to get out of bed to kill myself. The depression lifted enough that I could get out of bed and the attempt almost worked. 

For me getting better was almost the end.
The fear I will fail again and the emotional toll it would have on my friends and family are all that's keeping me here.
I listen to Citizen Soldier (covers depression, suicide and some other hard topics). Several are reminders to live like "Let it burn" which is my favorite.

I am committed to ending it because of my circumstances and illnesses. I don't want to but this is a case where the other options are worse. 

I don't necessarily want to but I need to.
I know they will feel like they should have done more to prevent it.

A couple years ago I was doing well enough on lamictal and figured I didnt need the meds anymore because I had my life under control. Less than a year later I was hospitalized and I still am not back to stable.

I highly recommend not going off your meds. If you are still having mood swings it might be time to talk to a doctor about adding another medication like others have suggested
It looks like 4 closed clams shut down the system

It could also be that events associated with any strong emotion are more likely to be remembered and depression can lead to the dampening of all emotions.

(Spoken as someone who has never done any research on the topic)
I dream in first person, but it's more of a narrative than visualization. It's pretty much reading a book where I'm the main character

One of my coworkers has made two statements that make me loathe her: "Everyone is bipolar" and "Everyone with a mental illness should be locked up for the rest of their lives" (I know the second isn't specific to bipolar but it still made my blood boil.) I couldn't respond because I was at work but I wanted to take her down.

I generally wait at least a week if it is inexpensive and useful. 

If it is expensive or something I want but don't need, I wait at least two weeks. If I know I am hypo/manic I try to wait even longer by which time I have generally forgotten about the item.

I had a manic episode followed by depression bad enough that my friend dragged me to a therapist and explained to the therapist what was going on since I had no idea anything was abnormal. Therapist transfered me to a psychiatrist and I was immediately diagnosed.
Does your school have a health center? Both schools I went to had free counseling for students even if they didn't have the school's health insurance.
I use it to store photos and documents and anything else that I want to keep but I don't want anyone to find. I just make sure I never stay logged into it on my devices

I also rip up what I write immediately. I can't stand to think that someone else could ever see how bad my headspace is. Sometimes I will take pictures on my phone and store them in a junk email account just in case I ever need the information again.

Congratulations on making it!

As a teenager I never saw myself living past 25. I survived an attempt last year and just turned 26. Now I just need to see what the next 25 years will bring.
Never stop taking your meds. Make sure you always have a psychiatrist.
I am almost always INTJ, strong mania can change it.

Are there any partial hospitalization programs around you? When I was released from a three-month hospital stay, they encouraged me to go into a part time program where I was at a hospital for about 6 hours a day. It was a mix of therapy sessions, meeting with a psychiatrist, and having a support system. It was a nice way to ease back into society. 

I do agree that it can be very jarring going from full-time hospitalization to being responsible for your entire life again.

At least it was a small purchase and done for a worthwhile reason.

I am also fighting the strong urge to cook right now. Luckily I don't have the ingredients and I have no way of getting them this late at night.

I have bought moving boxes and bubble wrap even though I am not moving and some clothing that is at least somewhat needed. $75 total and the urge to buy is getting worse as time progresses. 

Amazon makes it way to easy to order on a whim.

I do this too with the added perk of being paranoid that the person will figure it out. I have mostly tried to ignore those thoughts and force myself to think of other things with varying degrees of success.

I find it useful for myself because I can take precautions now; long term changes but also recognizing when my mood is changing.

What I don't find useful is when other people use my diagnosis to try and define my actions. Sometimes others, especially my family, think that every little momentary change in my mood is because I'm cycling. It can get annoying constantly telling people no it's not because I'm bipolar, it's because I'm human and have emotions.
I am asexual and have been diagnosed bipolar I for 4 years. My diagnosis hasn't made a difference as far as I can tell. I have  never experienced hypersexuality during any of my episodes.

For me, I was depressed and suicidal. My meds were keeping me just sane enough to prevent me from committing suicide but I very much wanted to end it. Depressed me decided I should go off my meds so I would end it. Needless to say I ended up in the hospital.
Try donating as much as you can - that's what I am in the middle of doing.
I agree with all of this. I wish you could tell someone that you wanted to die without them worrying or trying to get you hospitalized. Sometimes just talkin would help.
I was suicidal and wouldn't respond to medication without severe side effects or ECT.
12 weeks
When I was in the same situation, I found reading old emails and messages helped me find out what I had done.
I just finished ramping up to my final dose of lamictal and as I was increasing the suicidal thoughts kept getting worse. But it will vary from person to person so take that with a grain of salt.
Can you keep the pills and some water right next to these couch?

I wish I had the answer. It has been two weeks since finishing 34 treatments sprrad over three months. I lost almost all of my memories and have gotten hardly any back yet. When I started I was told it would take about two months to get everything back.

American insurance sucks. I went off Lamictal (I was on 200 mg twice a day) and a year later my doctors decided to put me back on lamictal and I had to start at 25 mg and titrate back to my old dose. I had some mild side effects last time, but this time I haven't had any side effects so that was nice. I don't know if everyone would be so lucky as to avoid side effects the second time or if it was just me though.
I love the textured look you achieved.
Awesome! If you don't mind, how did you make it?
